name.en: The Canyon Rim Trail & Perrine Bridge Gateway

summary.en: Windswept, dramatic, and inspiring, this area is an open-air museum where raw nature, daredevil history, and engineering marvels converge.

description.en: A world-famous stage for extreme sports, this is the only man-made structure in the U.S. where BASE jumping is legal year-round without a permit, 486 feet above the Snake River.

name.en: Evel Knievel's Snake River Canyon Jump Site

description.en: A monument to glorious failure, this large earthen ramp is the exact spot where the daredevil attempted to launch his steam-powered 'Sky-Cycle' across the canyon in 1974.
Known as the 'Niagara of the West,' this geological marvel is 45 feet taller than its famous counterpart, thundering over a 900-foot-wide rim of basalt.
A hidden history lesson where one of the city's namesake falls was sacrificed for hydroelectric power, leaving a poignant reminder of the negotiation between nature and industry.

prompt.en: Take a photo that captures the immense scale and depth of the Snake River Canyon from the trail.
The canyon rim is known for its wind. Take a selfie that shows your hair blowing in the breeze.
Strike a pose like a daredevil about to take on the canyon. Be safe and stay behind the railings!
Find a safe spot to watch for BASE jumpers from the Perrine Bridge. Can you capture a photo of one in mid-air?
Take a photo looking straight down at the Snake River, trying to make it look like a tiny ribbon.
Find an interesting rock formation along the canyon wall and take a close-up photo of its texture.
Locate an informational plaque along the trail and take a photo of the most interesting fact you learn.
Take a short video and try to capture the sound of the wind whistling over the canyon's edge.
Use the steel arches of the Perrine Bridge to frame a beautiful shot of the canyon beyond it.
Find a wildflower, a hardy shrub, or a piece of sagebrush growing near the rim and take an artistic photo of it with the canyon blurred in the background.
Capture a photo of your own shadow stretching out over the canyon rim.
Look to the skies! Can you spot a hawk, eagle, or other bird of prey soaring on the updrafts? Try to get a picture.
